note: A Stop-event hook (hooks/before_stop.py) mechanizing 'claim only what you derived from the tree' at the moment a turn ends: it flags a completion claim (done/fixed/passing) carrying no evidence of a run. Clean-room from vibeguard (MIT); no text copied. Built by a subagent, integrated here.

decisions.question: Should a Stop-time completion-claim guard block or advise?
decisions.commitment: Advise by default; deny only a hard 'all tests pass'-class claim with zero evidence, and only once (it downgrades to advisory when stop_hook_active is set, so the block fires once and the turn can still end).
decisions.why: A Stop hook that hard-blocks can trap a session in a loop, and a trap is the exact thing that gets a hook deleted — the lesson before_write already records. So a soft claim returns allow-with-a-reminder and only a sweeping suite-is-green assertion backed by nothing denies. Nestor has a documented history of green-suite claims the tree did not support, which is why that class earns the harder default.

decisions.question: What separates a claim that passes from one that gets flagged?
decisions.commitment: A quoted run: a code span with a command word, 'N passed', an exit code, or file.py:line. Claim present and evidence absent is the only flagged state; the guard fails OPEN when it cannot find the final message.
decisions.why: The rule is about evidence, not vocabulary — 'done' beside `pytest -q -> 1011 passed` is fine, 'all tests pass' beside nothing is not. Closed on its subject, open on its own parsing bug, opposite defaults on purpose; a mutation making evidence always-present drops four tests.
